dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between strong and nearly absent eclipses every other orbit and its depth varies by more than threefold between sectors and even within the same pipeline. Three deep events carry most of the signal while the rest are flat to negative. Combined with a nearby faint star capable of mimicking the dip, this favours a blended eclipsing binary at about 26 days over a small planet on the target.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ at >9 sigma, positive difference 440.7 ppm in 3 sectors (sector_oe_max_sigma 11.9, sector_oe_same_sign_share 0.8571). This is a binary at twice the period, not a planet.
reasons.value: 9.582 (depth ratio 7.6, odd 507.7 ppm vs even 67.03 ppm)

reasons.why: Depth truly changes within the same light-curve product, inconsistent with a quiet planet transiting the target star.
